standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of an abelian sheaf on a site computed from an injective resolution
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard in this chapter: H^p(U, F) is the p-th cohomology of the complex of sections of an injective resolution F -> I^bullet
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the representative of the class and the fact that restriction is computed on representatives; the covering argument is the counted content.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of the resolution in positive degrees means local triviality of sections of the kernel
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard sheaf theory: I^{p-1} -> I^p -> I^{p+1} exact in Ab(C) means a section over U killed by d becomes a coboundary after restriction to a covering
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the existence of the local primitives xi_i; identifying them and concluding the vanishing is inside the counted proof.

core_obligations: Choose a representative: take an injective resolution F -> I^bullet, so that the class xi in H^p(U, F) is represented by a cocycle tilde xi in I^p(U) with d^p(tilde xi) = 0 (proof lines 2264-2266).

Find local primitives: the hypothesis p > 0 makes the sequence I^{p-1} -> I^p -> I^{p+1} exact in Ab(C) at I^p, so there is a covering U = {U_i -> U} with tilde xi|_{U_i} = d^{p-1}(xi_i) for some xi_i in I^{p-1}(U_i) (proof lines 2266-2271).
Conclude that the class dies: the restricted class xi|_{U_i} is represented by the restricted cocycle tilde xi|_{U_i}, which is a coboundary, hence xi|_{U_i} = 0 for every i (proof lines 2271-2276).
proof_roadmap: Resolve the sheaf injectively and represent the class by an explicit cocycle (proof lines 2264-2266).
Use exactness at I^p to make the representative locally a coboundary on some covering (proof lines 2266-2271).
Read off the vanishing of the restricted class on that covering (proof lines 2271-2276).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for any site C, abelian sheaf F, object U, degree p > 0 and class xi in H^p(U, F) there is a covering of U over which xi restricts to zero (statement lines 2256-2260). The proof has to move once from the class to a representative and once from the representative to local primitives, and the second move is available precisely because p > 0 makes the resolution exact at I^p, so a section of the kernel sheaf becomes a coboundary after restriction to a covering (proof lines 2264-2271). The statement is then immediate from the fact that the restriction of a class is computed from the restriction of its representative. The claim is H2: the same two-step use of an injective resolution as in the ringed-site version, with its own self-contained proof in this chapter.
